title: The Invisible Man
author: H. G. Wells
summary: Num dia frio de fevereiro, um estranho chega a uma pequena vila inglesa com o rosto todo coberto por ataduras, óculos escuros e luvas. Ele se tranca no quarto da pousada com suas garrafas de produtos químicos, e logo coisas estranhas começam a acontecer na vila. Quem é esse homem, e o que ele esconde debaixo das ataduras?

chapters.title: The Stranger
paragraphs: The stranger came early in February, on a cold, snowy day. He walked from the railway station to the village of Iping, carrying a small black bag. He was covered from head to foot. He wore a thick coat, a big hat, gloves and dark blue glasses. There was not one centimetre of his skin to see.
He walked into the Coach and Horses inn. “A fire!” he cried. “A room and a fire!”
Mrs Hall, the landlady, was very happy. Visitors were rare in Iping in winter. She lit a fire in the best room and brought him some lunch. But the stranger did not take off his hat or his coat.
“Can I take your coat to dry it, sir?” she asked.
“No,” he said, and he did not turn round.

When she came back later, he had taken off his hat. She almost dropped the plates. His whole head was covered in white bandages. Only his pink nose was showing, and it was very shiny. He held a napkin in front of his mouth.
“Poor man,” thought Mrs Hall. “He's had an accident. Maybe his face is badly burned.”

The next day a lot of luggage arrived for him: boxes of books and many, many bottles. The stranger took out the bottles at once and put them everywhere. They were full of chemicals. Straw from the boxes lay all over the floor.
“I'm doing experiments,” he said to Mrs Hall. “I don't want anyone to disturb me. Do you understand? Nobody.”
“Of course, sir,” said Mrs Hall. He paid well, so she did not complain. But the people of Iping began to talk.
“He's a criminal and he's hiding from the police,” said some.
“He's a poor man with a terrible face,” said others.
The children called him the Bogey Man and ran away when he walked past.

chapters.title: Strange Things in Iping
paragraphs: The stranger worked in his room day and night. Sometimes the people in the inn heard him talking angrily to himself. Sometimes they heard glass breaking.

One afternoon Teddy Henfrey, the clock repairer, came to repair the clock in the stranger's room. He worked very slowly, because he wanted to look at the stranger. The dark glasses seemed to stare at him like the eyes of a big fish.
“Are you finished?” said the stranger coldly. “Then go.”
Teddy left, red in the face. “There's something wrong with that man,” he told everyone.

A few days later, Mr Cuss, the village doctor, decided to visit the stranger. He wanted to know about the bandages. He knocked, went in, and closed the door. Ten minutes later he ran out of the room, very pale, and went straight to the vicar's house.

“Listen to me,” he said to the vicar. “I asked him about his hand. He laughed and put his arm towards me. There was no hand in the sleeve! It was empty. I could see right down it. And then something I couldn't see took my nose and pinched it. Hard!”
The vicar laughed. “You've been working too hard, Cuss,” he said. But the doctor did not laugh.

In April the money stopped. The stranger did not pay his bill. Then, on Whit Monday, there was a robbery at the vicar's house. Very early in the morning, the vicar and his wife heard someone downstairs. The vicar took a poker and went down quietly. He heard the sound of money from his desk. He looked into the room, but it was empty. Nobody was there!
“Who's there?” he cried. Nobody answered. But a moment later somebody sneezed in the hall, and the front door opened and closed by itself. The money was gone.

On the same morning, Mr and Mrs Hall saw that the stranger's door was open. The room was empty. His clothes and bandages were on the chair. Then the strangest thing happened. The hat jumped from the bed and flew at Mrs Hall's face. The chair rose into the air and pushed them out of the room. The door shut behind them.
Mrs Hall screamed. “It's the spirits!” she cried. “He has put the devil into my furniture!”
Later the stranger came back, though nobody saw him go in. Mrs Hall stood at his door. “You must pay your bill,” she said, “and you must tell me what you did to my furniture.”

chapters.title: No Head
paragraphs: The stranger came out of his room. “You want to know who I am?” he shouted. “I'll show you!”

He took off his glasses and pulled off his nose. It was made of pink cardboard, and it fell to the floor. Then he unwound the bandages from his face. The people in the bar screamed and ran to the door. Under the bandages there was nothing. The man had no head! There was only a coat and a collar, with nothing inside.
The village policeman, Mr Jaffers, arrived. “I've come to arrest you,” he said bravely. “Head or no head.”

The stranger took off his gloves. There were no hands. Jaffers took hold of an empty sleeve, but a hand he could not see hit him in the face. The stranger took off his coat, his shirt and his trousers. Now he was completely invisible. A great fight began. Men fell over, chairs flew, and nobody could see who to hit. Then Jaffers fell to the ground, and the invisible man ran out of the inn.
Outside, on the road, he met a tramp called Thomas Marvel. Marvel was sitting by the road, looking at some old boots.
“Those are terrible boots,” said a voice.
Marvel looked round. There was nobody there. “I'm going mad,” he said.

A stone flew through the air and hit him on the foot. “You're not mad,” said the voice. “I'm an invisible man. I need your help. I need someone to carry things for me and get me food and clothes. Help me, and I'll make you rich. Refuse, and I'll hurt you.”
“Why me?” asked Marvel in a weak voice.
“Because you're poor, and nobody will miss you,” said the voice. “And because I'm cold and hungry, and you have eyes that people can see. Now stand up. We're going back to Iping.”
Marvel was too frightened to say no. That night he went back to Iping and came out of the inn with the stranger's three books under his arm. They were the scientist's notebooks, full of his secrets.

chapters.title: Mr Marvel Runs Away
paragraphs: For several days Marvel walked along the roads with the books. The invisible man was always next to him. Whenever Marvel tried to run, a hand took his collar.

In the town of Port Stowe, Marvel sat on a bench outside an inn. A sailor sat down next to him with a newspaper. “Have you heard about the invisible man?” said the sailor. “He attacked a policeman in Iping. They say he's here, in this part of the country.”
Marvel's face became white. Then a voice spoke in his ear, very quietly. “Don't say a word, or I'll kill you.”

Marvel now had a lot of money in his pockets. Banks and shops near him were losing money, and nobody knew why. But Marvel was very unhappy. One day he saw his chance. He ran as fast as he could to the Jolly Cricketers, an inn at Port Burdock.
“The invisible man!” he shouted. “He's after me! Help me! Hide me!”

The barman pushed Marvel into a back room and locked the door. A moment later the glass in the window broke. The bar door opened, and nobody came in. There were policemen and customers in the bar. They tried to catch the invisible man. A policeman fired his gun five times into the empty air. Somebody shouted with pain. Then everything was silent, and the invisible man was gone.
Marvel was safe, but the invisible man was wounded and very angry. That night he went into a big house on the hill above Port Burdock. A light was on in the study, where a doctor was working late.

The doctor's name was Kemp. He was a scientist, and he hoped one day to be famous. He went up to his bedroom and saw blood on the door handle. Then he saw a bandage, moving on its own in the air above the bed.
Kemp stood very still. “Who's there?” he said.
“Kemp!” said a voice. “Don't be afraid. I'm Griffin. We studied together at university.”

chapters.title: Griffin's Story
paragraphs: Kemp gave Griffin a dressing gown, some food and a bed. The empty dressing gown sat in a chair and ate. It was a strange thing to watch. In the morning Griffin told him his story.

“At university I studied light,” he said. “You remember that I'm an albino. I have white skin, white hair and pink eyes. I wanted to make the body as clear as glass. If light goes straight through a thing, you can't see it. I worked on this for years.
“I had no money. So I took my father's money, and it wasn't his. He killed himself because of the debt. I didn't even feel sorry. I only wanted to finish my work.

“First I made a piece of cloth invisible. Then a white cat. It was easy, except for its eyes. Then I took the drugs myself. It was terrible. My body burned with pain all night. In the morning I looked at my hands. They were like glass, and slowly they disappeared completely.
“My landlord came to my room to ask about the cat. I set fire to the house to destroy my machines, and I left. I thought I was the most powerful man in the world. But I was wrong.

“It was January. I was naked and very cold in the snowy streets. People walked into me. Dogs could smell me. When I ate, people could see the food inside me until it disappeared. I went into a big shop and slept there, but in the morning I had to escape. Then I found a small shop for actors' costumes. There I took clothes, a false nose, glasses and bandages. I went to Iping because I wanted a quiet place to find a cure. But those stupid villagers wouldn't leave me alone.”
Kemp listened carefully. And while Griffin talked, Kemp quietly wrote a letter.

chapters.title: The Reign of Terror
paragraphs: “Now I need a partner,” said Griffin. “Marvel was a fool, but you're a scientist. With your help, I can do anything. We'll start a Reign of Terror. I'll take a town, like Burdock, and frighten everyone. People will obey me, and anyone who doesn't obey me will die.”
Kemp was horrified. He looked out of the window and saw three men walking up to the house. “Kemp, what's that?” cried Griffin. He understood at once. “You've betrayed me!”

The men were Colonel Adye, the chief of police, and two policemen. Kemp had sent his letter to them. The invisible man threw off the dressing gown and ran down the stairs. He knocked over Adye and was gone.

Kemp spoke to Adye seriously. “He's mad,” he said. “He wants to rule by fear. We must catch him. Close every door and window. Put flour on the floors, so we can see his feet. Keep dogs everywhere. He must eat and sleep. We must give him no food and no rest.”

Soon there were police and soldiers on every road. People locked their doors. That afternoon a man called Mr Wicksteed was walking home. He saw an iron bar moving through the air. He followed it to see what it was, and the invisible man killed him with it.

The next day Kemp received a letter. “The Reign of Terror begins today,” it said. “This is day one of the new world. I will kill one man as a lesson to everyone. His name is Kemp. He can lock his doors and hide, but death is coming for him. Today. — The Invisible Man.”
Kemp read the letter twice. He was afraid, but he was also determined. “This is our chance,” he said. “He'll come to me, and we'll be ready.”

chapters.title: The End of the Invisible Man
paragraphs: Colonel Adye came to the house again. As he left, the invisible man took his gun and shot him. Then Griffin attacked the house. He broke the windows one by one with an axe. Two policemen inside tried to fight him with pokers. The axe flew through the air, and the house was full of crashing glass.

Kemp jumped out of a back window and ran. He ran down the hill towards the town. He had never run so fast in his life. Behind him on the road he heard the sound of bare feet. They were coming closer and closer.
“The invisible man!” he shouted. “He's coming! Help!”

People heard him. Men came out of their houses with sticks. At the bottom of the hill, near the Jolly Cricketers, some workmen were digging the road. Kemp ran towards them, and then something hit him and he fell. Invisible hands closed around his throat.

“I've got him!” shouted Kemp. A big workman jumped forward with a spade and hit the air above Kemp. There was a cry of pain. Then all the men threw themselves on the invisible body. They kicked and hit it until it lay still.
“Stop!” cried Kemp. “He's hurt! Stand back!”

Kemp put his hand on the chest. The heart was not beating. Griffin was dead. And then a strange thing happened. Slowly, the body began to appear. First they saw the thin white nerves, like a drawing in pencil. Then the bones, then the flesh and skin. At last a young man lay on the ground. His hair was white and his eyes were pink, and his face was full of anger and pain.
“Cover his face!” cried a woman. “For God's sake, cover his face!”

Griffin was dead, but his notebooks were not lost. Mr Marvel still had them. Today he is the owner of a little inn. Late at night he takes out the books and reads them. He can't understand the science, but he dreams of the wonderful secrets inside them. And he never tells anyone that he has them.
